newsitem.title: INDIA: India Chidambaram's party withholds move on rule.
newsitem.headline: India Chidambaram's party withholds move on rule.

text.p: The leader of former finance minister P. Chidambaram's party on Monday withheld a decision on whether to join the new federal government as tensions with a regional rival mounted.

Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) chief G.K. Moopanar consulted with party leaders in the southern city of Madras over the decision on whether to enter new Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's week-old government.

The TMC dealt a blow to Gujral on April 19 when it tentatively decided to stay out of the centre-left government because the United Front coalition passed over Moopanar in favour of Gujral as its leader and prime minister

The regional party authorised Moopanar on Sunday to take a final decision after cadres strongly recommended staying out of Gujral's cabinet and concentrating on fighting its rival, Tamil Nadu state's ruling Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK).
Moopanar had been expected to announce a decision on Monday or Tuesday.
But party officials said he might wait until the shock waves from a corruption scandal that rocked Gujral's Janata Dal party had dissipated before taking a decision.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said on Monday that it had decided to prosecute Janata Dal chief Laloo Prasad Yadav and 55 others in an investigation into a $280 million animal fodder scandal. Yadav has said he is innocent.
The Janata Dal is the biggest party in Gujral's United Front coalition with 45 of the alliance's 178 deputies in the 545-member lower house of parliament.
The TMC is the third biggest component in the 15-party United Front with 20 seats.
"He (Moopanar) will probably wait until the situation with the fodder scandal clears before he makes a move," a TMC official said.
On Sunday, some TMC activists burned an effigy of Industry Minister Murasoli Maran, a DMK leader accused by TMC rivals of helping to scuttle Moopanar's chances of becoming prime minister.
Some DMK members retaliated on Monday by burning an effigy of TMC leader Chidambaram.
Chidambaram was finance minister under Gujral's ousted predecessor, former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Gujral has retained the finance minister position for himself, apparently so that he could award it to Chidambaram if his party decided to join the government.
